questions.question: D1 — Pass 2/3/5: The plan identifies that saving takes 2-5 seconds with no feedback (frozen page). DESIGN.MD fully specifies the fix: inline spinner beside "Saving…" inside the disabled Save button, aria-busy=true, reduced-motion support. The plan names this as a gap but adds no implementation task. Should we add it? <gstack-qid:plan-design-review-save-spinner>

options.label: Add implementation task (Recommended)
options.description: Add a concrete task: apply DESIGN.MD pending-state pattern — spinner + 'Saving…' in disabled button, aria-busy=true, prefers-reduced-motion support. Fix: ~30 min CC / ~2h human. Resolves Issues 2.1, 3 (step 6 emotional arc), and 5.5 in one task.

options.label: Leave as gap description
options.description: Keep the gap named but untasked. Developer reads the plan gap section and decides implementation during build. Risk: the pattern is non-trivial and may ship without reduced-motion support.

questions.question: D2 — Pass 5: Visual Hierarchy. Save, Reset, Cancel, and Export are all rendered identically — same size, weight, and color. Nothing signals which is primary. DESIGN.MD specifies: Save is the only filled primary action (#1d4ed8 bg, white text); Reset, Cancel, Export are neutral ghost buttons. The plan names this gap but adds no implementation task. Should we add it? <gstack-qid:plan-design-review-primary-button>

options.label: Add implementation task (Recommended)
options.description: Add task: Apply Button primary variant (#1d4ed8 fill, white text) to Save; ghost variant to Reset, Cancel, Export. Fix aligns with DESIGN.MD exactly. ~15 min CC / ~1h human. Resolves Issue 5.1.

options.label: Leave as gap description
options.description: Keep gap named but untasked. Risk: developer ships all four buttons identical, user has no visual cue which action is primary — most critical UX gap on this page.

questions.question: D3 — Pass 5: Spacing. The plan reports 16px spacing appearing in a third location, alongside 24px (field groups) and 32px (sections) which match DESIGN.MD. But the plan doesn't say WHERE the 16px appears. DESIGN.MD's scale has no 16px slot: sections=32px, field groups=24px, label-to-input=8px. How should we handle this? <gstack-qid:plan-design-review-spacing-16px>

options.label: Add task to locate and correct 16px spacing (Recommended)
options.description: Add task: audit spacing in the header action group and between InlineStatus and first fieldset — most likely candidates for the 16px outlier. Replace with the correct DESIGN.MD value (8px, 24px, or 32px depending on context). ~20 min CC / ~30 min human.

options.label: Leave location ambiguous
options.description: Keep gap named without specifying location. Developer hunts during implementation. Risk: they fix the wrong instance, or the 16px inconsistency survives because its location was never pinned.

options.label: Escalate — need clarification on exact location
options.description: Pause for the user to identify which spacing element uses 16px. Safest if you know where it is. Adds one more conversation round before work begins.

answers.D3 \u2014 Pass 5: Spacing. The plan repo: Add task to locate and correct 16px spacing (Recommended)

questions.question: D4 — Pass 5/6: Error Color — WCAG AA failure. The current error style (red text on light pink background) has ~3:1 contrast. WCAG AA requires 4.5:1 for normal-weight text. This fails both accessibility law and DESIGN.MD, which specifies: error.text #991b1b on error.surface #fef2f2, with an icon and explicit text. The plan names the gap but adds no implementation task. Should we add it? <gstack-qid:plan-design-review-error-contrast>

options.label: Add implementation task (Recommended)
options.description: Add task: Set error text to #991b1b on #fef2f2 background, add icon + explicit error text label. Fixes both the WCAG AA violation and DESIGN.MD alignment. ~15 min CC / ~1h human. Resolves Issues 5.3 and 6.1.

options.label: Leave as gap description
options.description: Keep gap named but untasked. Risk: WCAG AA violation ships — legal and accessibility liability, plus poor experience for users with low vision or in challenging lighting.

questions.question: D5 — Pass 5: Typography. Three font sizes are used (14px, 16px, 18px) across form labels. DESIGN.MD specifies two roles only: 16px body/form labels/helper text; 20px section headings. The 14px violates the Universal Rule (body text must be ≥16px) and WCAG readability. The 18px conflicts with section heading size (20px) creating a muddled hierarchy. Should we add a consolidation task? <gstack-qid:plan-design-review-typography-sizes>

options.label: Add implementation task (Recommended)
options.description: Add task: audit all form label and helper text sizes; replace 14px with 16px and 18px with 16px or 20px depending on element role. Verify no occurrence of 14px or 18px ships. ~20 min CC / ~1h human. Resolves Issue 5.4 and the <16px universal rule violation.

options.label: Leave as gap description
options.description: Keep gap named but untasked. Risk: 14px text ships (below minimum; violates Universal Rules), and the muddled 18px/20px near-match confuses hierarchy for sighted users and may confuse screen reader users too.

questions.question: D6 — Pass 6: Reduced-motion save behavior. The plan says 'Respect reduced motion' and DESIGN.MD says the spinner has 'reduced-motion support' — but neither specifies what the user actually sees when prefers-reduced-motion: reduce is active. An animated spinner that ignores reduced-motion ships a broken accessibility experience. Which behavior should be specified? <gstack-qid:plan-design-review-reduced-motion>

options.label: Static spinner + 'Saving…' text (Recommended)
options.description: Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, render the spinner as a static (non-animating) icon beside 'Saving…'. Users still get visual feedback but no motion. Matches what most spinner libraries produce under reduced-motion.

options.label: 'Saving…' text only, no spinner
options.description: Hide the spinner entirely under reduced-motion; show 'Saving…' text alone inside the disabled button. Simpler, zero animation artifacts, but removes the visual progress indicator entirely.

questions.question: D7 — Pass 7: InlineStatus layout stability. The persistent status area transitions between three states: blank (before first save), 'Unsaved changes', and 'Saved at HH:mm'. If no minimum height is reserved, the content below it (Profile fieldset) will shift up/down each time the text appears or disappears. Neither the plan nor DESIGN.MD specifies whether a min-height should hold the space. What should the plan specify? <gstack-qid:plan-design-review-inline-status-height>

options.label: Reserve min-height equal to one text line (Recommended)
options.description: Add spec: InlineStatus container has min-height: 1 line-height (approximately 24px). Blank state renders empty space; text transitions without layout shift. Matches the 'Unsaved changes' line height as the stable baseline.

options.label: Allow layout shift (no min-height)
options.description: No min-height; content shifts when status text appears. Simpler CSS. Risk: noticeable layout jump on first edit or save — may feel broken, especially combined with the focus ring on the Save button.

options.label: Defer — decide during implementation
options.description: Leave this unspecified; let the developer decide during build. Risk: inconsistent between future form pages if not codified.

answers.D7 \u2014 Pass 7: InlineStatus layout st: Reserve min-height equal to one text line (Recommended)

The design review added significant interaction specs (spinner pending-state, reduced-motion behavior, layout stability) that have architectural implications. Eng review is the required shipping gate. What next? <gstack-qid:plan-design-review-next-step>
